properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23, and he flagged it for checking himself: "may have to verify this statement against true systems engineering doctrine."

HIS WORDS: "I believe a capability is a set of functions working together to deliver that capability. Black boxes deliver functionality, not necessarily a capability... then capabilities can be expressed at subsystem_B.component_1 (delivers function_K) <--> subsystem_A.component_2 (delivers function_L) <--> subsystem_C.component_5 (delivers function_J)... function_K + function_L + function_J = capability_R."

✅ THE DOCTRINE CHECK HE ASKED FOR, and it supports him. UAF places Capability in the STRATEGIC domain — an ability to achieve a desired effect under specified standards and conditions — and it is realized by a CONFIGURATION of resources performing functions, never owned by one resource. DoDAF says the same through its matrices: CV-6 maps Capability to Operational Activities, and SV-5a is literally the Operational-Activity-to-Systems-Function traceability matrix — an N-to-N mapping, which only exists because one capability spans many functions across many systems. So 'a black box performs functions; a capability emerges from functions across boxes' is the doctrinal position, not a deviation from it.

🛑 AND IT CONTRADICTS WHAT REFLOW2 DOES TODAY, which is why this matters more than the other two. Measured 2026-08-23: there is NO `Function` node type in the schema (29 types, none of them Function). Capability is joined to Component by ALLOCATED_TO, and `fact:reflow2s-black-boxes-hold-no-functions-allocation-went-straight-to-the-modules` measured 177 of 178 ALLOCATED_TO edges pointing at a MODULE, one at a subsystem, and DECOMPOSES at ZERO. reflow2 currently models a capability as belonging to ONE part. Under his reading that is the wrong shape: it collapses the function layer out and makes a capability something a box owns rather than something a configuration achieves.

THE OPTIONS:
(a) ADD A `Function` NODE TYPE. Component PERFORMS Function; Capability is COMPOSED OF Functions. Doctrinally clean and it makes his three-part example expressible. COUNTER: a schema change is the most expensive kind here — it needs an upgrade doc and a foundation migration — and 182 existing allocations would have to mean something afterwards.
(b) LET A CAPABILITY BE ALLOCATED TO SEVERAL COMPONENTS and read the set as the configuration. Cheap; no schema change; the edge already permits it. COUNTER: it loses WHICH function each part contributes, which is the whole content of his example — K, L and J are not interchangeable.
(c) TREAT `Flow` AS THE FUNCTION LAYER. It already models an ordered process with steps and roled transitions. COUNTER: a Flow is a SEQUENCE and a capability is not necessarily sequential; forcing one into the other would misrepresent both.
(d) DO NOTHING — one-part allocation is a simplification reflow2 chose, and it is adequate for the projects it serves.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any USER of reflow2 has hit this. Every measurement behind it is from reflow2's own design, and `reflow2 is a wrench` says the test is whether a user's project needs it — nobody has asked that question yet.
properties.name: OPEN — is a capability a SET OF FUNCTIONS across several parts, with a black box delivering functions rather than capabilities? It would need a Function type reflow2 does not have
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Kept separate from the nesting and contract-level questions because it is the only one of the three that would change the SCHEMA, and it can be answered no whatever the other two decide.
